newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on Tokyo sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on Tokyo sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended lower on Monday following healthy sales from traders at the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) on a firmer yen, dealers said.
"Basically it's all TOCOM-related selling on a stronger yen," said one dealer at an international bank.
Bullion ended at US$347.30/80 an ounce against New York's US$348.50/349.00 close on Friday.
Trading was largely quiet, with good support seen at $347 per ounce, dealers said.
Bullion dealers said if gold fell below $346 per ounce in overnight trade, it could slide much further, but if not, it would likely bounce back up to $350 per ounce.
Local gold ended HK$1 higher at HK$3,218 a tael.
Physical demand had picked up, dealers said.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -1.00 from -4.00
